sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Every setting the app reads
sections.what: Lists the database address, login secret, public site address, cricket score key, admin emails, cron secret, destructive reseed switch, setup password, feature switches, and Gemini keys and prices. Empty values mean the feature is off or a value must be filled in.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a new developer copy it and fill in the names without guessing.
sections.watch_out: The placeholder admin email must be replaced, and the destructive reseed switch must stay false in production.

summary: A template listing every setting the app reads, with safe placeholder values to copy into a local settings file.
purpose: Document the settings and give safe defaults for local work.
why: The comments explain which settings are required, optional or dangerous. Likely reason: a template makes setup repeatable for any developer.
how: 1) Copy it to a local settings file. 2) Fill in required values such as the secret and the admin email. 3) Leave optional values empty. 4) Start the app, which reads the file.
inputs: Values typed in by the developer.
outputs: Nothing directly; the app and setup scripts read the copied file.
risks: The local database password is a known default, acceptable only for local use. An empty secret stops production from starting. Turning on the destructive reseed in production would erase data.
debug: If the app refuses to start, check NEXTAUTH_SECRET. If sign-in redirects fail, check NEXTAUTH_URL is a full address. If a feature is missing, check its switch and key.
